readings.text: בְּעִטְרָן מִפְּנֵי כְּבוֹד הַשַּׁ… / מְשַׁמְּנִין בְּשֶׁמֶן אֱגוֹזִים בְּ…
decisions: kevod: the kaf has a dot inside it (a dagesh) and a shva under it, so it reads כְּבוֹד. The holam on the vav is visible.
Both words that begin with bet have a dagesh and a shva: בְּעִטְרָן and בְּשֶׁמֶן.
unresolved: The mark under the ayin of the first word is blurred. It is either a hiriq or a hataf; I chose hiriq, but with low confidence.
The top line is clipped and was not read.

readings.text: …תָּן. וְכָל הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הָעֵץ אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא טֻמְאַת / …תִילַת הַבֶּגֶד שֶׁקִּפְּלָהּ וְלֹא הִבְהֲבָהּ, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר / מַדְלִיקִין בָּהּ, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר טְהוֹרָה הִיא,
decisions: mitamme: the first mem has a shva under it. The tet has a patah and no visible dagesh. The second mem has a dagesh and a tsere, followed by an unpointed alef: מְטַמֵּא.
hivhavah: the final he has a mappiq (הִבְהֲבָהּ), and a comma follows it.
bah: the bet has a dagesh and a qamats, the he has a mappiq (בָּהּ), and a comma follows it.
unresolved: Under the first mem of mitamme, I cannot fully rule out a hiriq instead of a shva. I chose shva.

readings.text: ד לֹא יִקּוֹב אָדָם שְׁפֹּפֶרֶת שֶׁל בֵּיצָה וִימַלְאֶנָּה שֶׁמֶן / …פִּי הַנֵּר בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁתְּהֵא מְנַטֶּפֶת וַאֲפִילוּ הִיא שֶׁל חֶרֶס,
decisions: yimall word: the consonants are ו־י־מ־ל־א־נ־ה. The pointing is vav with hiriq, unpointed yod, mem with patah, lamed with shva, alef with segol, nun with dagesh and qamats, then he: וִימַלְאֶנָּה.
shfoferet: the consonants are ש־פ־פ־ר־ת, with no vav. The pointing is shin with shva, first pe with dagesh and a holam dot, second pe with segol, resh with segol: שְׁפֹּפֶרֶת.
unresolved: I cannot tell whether the lamed of the yimall word has a dagesh. None is visible at this resolution.
In shfoferet, the dot on the first pe could be a holam or a dagesh, and it may be both. I read it as both.

readings.text: הַפְּתִילָה בְּתוֹכָהּ בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁתְּהֵא שׁוֹאֶבֶת, / ה הַמְכַבֶּה אֶת הַנֵּר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מִתְיָרֵא מִפְּ…
decisions: betokhah: the bet has a dagesh and a shva, and the final he has a mappiq: בְּתוֹכָהּ.

readings.text: …רוּחַ רָעָה אוֹ בִּשְׁבִיל הַחוֹלֶה שֶׁיִּישַׁן, פָּטוּר. כְּחָ… / עַל הַשֶּׁמֶן כְּחָס עַל הַפְּתִילָה חַיָּב. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי פּוֹטֵר / …תִילָה מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא עוֹשָׂה פֶּחָם: ו עַל שָׁלֹשׁ עֲ… / בִּשְׁעַת לֵדָתָן, עַל שֶׁאֵינָן זְהִירוֹת בְּנִדָּה בְּחַלָּה וּבְהַ…
decisions: bishvil: the first bet has a dagesh and a hiriq, the shin has a shva, and the second bet has no dagesh: בִּשְׁבִיל.
oseh: the ayin has a holam vav, and the sin (dot on the left) has a qamats: עוֹשָׂה.
pecham: the pe has a dagesh and a segol, and the het has a qamats: פֶּחָם. A sof pasuq (:) follows it.
unresolved: In oseh, a speck inside the final he could be a mappiq. I did not record it.

readings.text: בָּעוֹלָם: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְכָל בָּנַיִךְ לִ… / בָּנַיִךְ אֶלָּא בּוֹנָיִךְ: שָׁלוֹם רָב … / שָׁלוֹם בְּחֵילֵךְ שַׁלְוָה בְּאַרְמְנוֹתָ…
decisions: Both occurrences of banayikh have a dagesh and a qamats in the bet: בָּנַיִךְ.
In bonayikh, the bet is followed by a holam vav: בּוֹנָיִךְ.
unresolved: In bonayikh, the dot inside the bet is faint, so the dagesh is not certain.
The third line is cropped at the bottom, so its vowels are not reliable.

readings.text: חַתן שַׁבָּת: / חר״ק וַיְכֻלּוּ הַשָּׁמַיִם וְהָאָרֶץ וְכָ…
decisions: Top rubric: I read חַתן שַׁבָּת followed by a colon. The shin has a patah and the bet has a dagesh and a qamats.
Speaker abbreviation: I read the small text before וַיְכֻלּוּ as חר״ק.
unresolved: Top rubric: the second letter may be ת or another letter, and the last letter may be a final nun or a closed letter. I cannot tell whether there is a dagesh or shva on it.
Speaker abbreviation: I cannot be sure the second letter is ר rather than ו, or exactly where the gershayim sits.

decisions: This abbreviation has the same letter shapes as the one in s35-0, so I give the same reading, חר״ק.
unresolved: Whether the second letter is ר or ו, and whether my right-to-left order of the letters is correct. The crop is small.

readings.text: בַּמֶּה מַדְלִיקִין וּבַמָּה אֵין מַדְלִיקִין, אֵין מַדְלִיקִי… / בְּחֹסֶן וְלֹא בְּכַלָּךְ, וְלֹא בִּפְתִילַת הָאִידָן וְלֹא בִּפְתִ…
decisions: uvammeh: the vav is a shuruq, the bet has a patah, and the mem has a dagesh and a qamats: וּבַמָּה.
The first word bammeh has a segol under the mem: בַּמֶּה.
unresolved: I read the second word on line 2 as בְּכַלָּךְ, but its letters are uncertain at this size.

readings.text: To a woman: לְשָׁנָה טוֹבָה תִּכָּתֵבִי: | To a man: לְשָׁנָה טוֹבָה תִּכָּתֵב: | To more than one woman: לְשָׁנָה טוֹבָה תִּכָּתֵבְנָה: | To more than one man: לְשָׁנָה טוֹבָה תִּכָּתֵבוּ:
decisions: Female plural greeting: the first tav has a dagesh and a hiriq, the kaf has a dagesh and a qamats, the second tav has a tsere, the bet has a shva, and the nun has a qamats: תִּכָּתֵבְנָה, followed by a colon.
unresolved: In the singular-woman and plural-man forms, the mark under the second tav could be a tsere or a shva.

readings.text: After the evening prayer but before עלינו the Kiddush is recited over a glass of wine. At home too, it is recited before the meal, but on the Sabbath preceded by ויכלו / בלחש וַיְהִי־עֶרֶב וַיְהִי־בֹקֶר בקול יוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי: וַיְכֻלּוּ הַשָּׁמַיִם וְהָאָרֶץ וְכָל־צְבָאָם: …
decisions: The Hebrew words in the English rubric are unpointed: עלינו and ויכלו.
Two small cue words are visible: one before וַיְהִי־עֶרֶב and one before יוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי. I transcribed them as בלחש and בקול.
unresolved: The first letter of both cue words (בלחש, בקול) is too small to tell bet from kaf. My transcription uses bet.

readings.text: זוּלָתוֹ. כַּכָּתוּב בְּתוֹ… / לְבָבֶךָ כִּי יְהֹוָה הוּא … / הָאָרֶץ מִתָּחַת אֵין עוֹ…
decisions: lekha kaf: in לְבָבֶךָ, the final kaf has a qamats inside it.
